_comment: Slakh2100 train split, pre-encoded with the streamgen accompaniment control at the CHOSEN silence cutoff of 0.85. THE CUTOFF LIVES HERE, NOT IN THE SBATCH: 'max_silence_fraction' is a config key so there is one place to change it, and the sbatch deliberately passes no --max_silence_fraction flag -- a CLI flag would silently win over this value and give two sources of truth. The pre-encode script prints the resolved filter at startup, so the job log still records what ran. 0.85 was decided 2026-09-09 by decoding two items from each 0.1-wide silence band (scripts/sample_silence_buckets.py) and listening; the earlier 0.3 came from 17 BabySlakh tracks and on Slakh sat below the corpus target median (0.346) and on the mode of its distribution, keeping only 56 of 270 validation and 252/240 of 1289 train items. At 0.85 the fraction limit is a backstop against near-empty windows -- the RMS floor's blind spot, since 99.9%% silence with one full-scale hit measures about -31 dBFS -- and it keeps ~784 of 1289 train items and an expected ~160-165 of 270 validation. Both splits MUST use the same value or they are not comparable. Window: pass --sample_size on the CLI, never as a key here (merge_config_into_args treats any argparse default that is not None as CLI-supplied, so a 'sample_size' key is silently ignored); the sbatch passes --sample_size 587853 --pad --batch_size 8, i.e. a 13.3s / 144-frame window from the START of every track (the pre-encode path sets random_crop=False). A silence fraction means something quite different at another window length -- 0.85 of 13.3s is about 2s of content, 0.85 of 380s is a minute. Augmentation: 'augment_variants' writes that many copies, variant 0 unaugmented and the rest each rolling a time-stretch rate from 'augment_time_stretch' and a pitch shift from +/- 'augment_pitch_semitones'; both go to the drums and the accompaniment with the same values ('augment_pitch_scope': 'all'), and the shared rate is what keeps them frame-aligned. Set 'augment_pitch_scope' to 'controls' to hold the drums at their original tuning while re-keying the accompaniment. Each variant is a fresh pass, so the stochastic stem submix is re-rolled per variant -- two encodes are therefore not bit-identical on the control side. Silence filtering: rejected and silent items are DROPPED, not replaced, leaving a gap in the latent ids; every surviving sidecar carries a 'levels' block (rms_dbfs, silence_fraction per stream) and '_skipped.json' records what went and why, per variant. Note the 'levels' block exists only for SURVIVORS, so this filtered encode cannot be used to re-choose its own cutoff -- read a new one off an encode with no fraction limit, via scripts/analyze_silence_levels.py. Inventory of which root holds which filter: docs/data/slakh-streamgen.md. Experiment: experiments/01-streamgen-conditioning/04-silence-filtering.md. Encode time and disk scale with the variant count.
